title: Ruairidh kneels first to the Cup
summary: At Seann Skell, Ruairidh, a sworn-man of the harbour-court, crosses the quay stones and kneels before his own son Mànas mac Ruairidh, the first of the preaching's hearers to do so. Six other net-menders kneel after him before the tide has gone out much further.

title: The harbour-court's scribe refuses the order's rite
summary: Donnchadh mac Ailein, scribe of the harbour-court at Seann Skell, refuses to enter the blessings of Òrd Mhanannain in Rolla a' Chalaidh beside the tallies of hulls and cargoes, holding a rite to be no business of a board kept for hulls. Mànas does not press the matter.

title: The first boats blessed at Cidhe an Diosail
summary: A dozen coasters are brought up one after another to Cidhe an Diosail at Seann Skell, and Mànas mac Ruairidh passes a plain wooden bowl of harbour water over each hull in turn, speaking the words that harden, within his own lifetime, into the fixed form of the rite of blessing.

title: Tidings of the king's death reach the quay
summary: A rider watering his horse at Seann Skell's harbour-court brings word that Lachlann mac Iain has died at Cathair dhearg, eighty-nine years old after a reign of fifty quiet years, and that his daughter Anna, fifty-four, has been crowned in his place. Mànas mac Ruairidh is not recorded to have said anything of it.

title: Tormod Ciar swears the Cup on the rope-walk
summary: At Cuan shean, the old rope-walker Tormod Ciar, told by a travelling net-mender what Mànas mac Ruairidh preaches of the mist, swears the Cup before his fellow walkers on the rope-walk itself, cupping rainwater in his own hands for want of a bowl, with no priest of the order present to hear him.

title: Taigh Mhanannain raised at Seann Skell
summary: Òrd Mhanannain raises its own house at Seann Skell, Taigh Mhanannain, low and built of the same grey stone as the quay near the old harbour-court. The congregation raises the silver for a proper cup without being asked, to replace the plain wooden bowl Mànas has used since the first blessing.

title: Death of Mànas mac Ruairidh
summary: Mànas mac Ruairidh dies at Seann Skell in the house he raised, six-and-thirty years after his first preaching on the quay, and is buried at his own asking under a plain slab facing the harbour mouth. Beathag nic Dhonnchaidh, who kept his house, keeps Taigh Mhanannain after him.

title: The rule of the headlands laid down
summary: After a winter's debate, the priests of Òrd Mhanannain at Ros bheag lay down that no boat of the faithful may sail out of sight of the headlands, on pain of answering for it before the Cup. The rule holds on the west coast far beyond any one preacher's lifetime.

title: Coinneach mac Sheumais turned back within the year
summary: Coinneach mac Sheumais, a skipper of Ros bheag, is turned back within the rule's first year by two of the order's own boats after taking his own boat further out than before, chasing a good run of fish. He never fishes so far out again.

title: Griogair cannot name his grandfather's star
summary: A priest of Òrd Mhanannain at Ros bheag asks a boy named Griogair, grandson of one of the last pilots to hold a course by night on that shore, which star his grandfather steered by. The boy cannot answer, and no one in his own house had thought to write the star's name down.

title: The granaries of Àth shean rebuilt
summary: The royal granaries at Àth shean, standing since before a' Scaradh, are pulled down and rebuilt in dressed stone on raised floors against the rats, along with a new tally-house. Fearchar mac Phàdraig, the reeve who oversees the three-year labour, sees the shire's grain stand dry through its first winter.

title: Birth of the fifth ruler of the house of Catrìona
summary: A child is born at Cathair dhearg to Anna's heir, then five-and-forty years old, in the six-and-twentieth year of Queen Anna's reign; Clàr nan Rìghrean keeps the year and not the name.

title: Death of Queen Anna
summary: Queen Anna dies at Cathair dhearg at five-and-eighty, one-and-thirty years crowned, the last of the house of Catrìona whose name Clàr nan Rìghrean keeps for more than a century.

title: The fourth ruler of the house of Catrìona crowned
summary: Anna's heir is crowned at Cathair dhearg within the season, fifty years old. Clàr nan Rìghrean keeps the reign's years and not its name.
